quest.title: Returning Curios
quest.description: Following Paimon's sage advice: "Chests of hidden Mora — gotta find 'em all!," you and Paimon decide to visit Idyia again, just to make sure you didn't miss any points of interest within Veluriyam Mirage. This turns out to be perfect timing, as Idyia has prepared something unique...
quest.rewards_formatted: Adventure EXP x100, Primogem x20, Mora x10000

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: This is it! This is the place we were locked up before...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: #Still remember how to open it, {NICKNAME}?

dialogues.speaker: Idyia
dialogues.text: #Oh, {NICKNAME}, Paimon! I was wondering where you two might be taking a stroll...

dialogues.speaker: Idyia
dialogues.text: Aha, let me see! A melody of pure water sings and twists around you, accompanied by the energy of gracefully dancing dewdrops! You two seem to be in good spirits.

dialogues.speaker: Idyia
dialogues.text: What do you say? Are you interested in sampling more of the delights of the "Veluriyam Mirage"?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hehe... Even Paimon didn't imagine that Idyia would start speaking more appropriately.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: She seems like a different person... Wait! Is she a different person? Are you another creation of Iydia...?

dialogues.speaker: Idyia
dialogues.text: My body has always been my own creation! Alright, that's enough talking about bygone days!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hey, Idyia seems much more lively. That's so wonderful!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wait, wait... What were we talking about?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Sampling the delights of the Veluriyam Mirage?

choices.text: Traveling around can lead to lots of pleasant surprises.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Exactly, great minds think alike! We'll want to explore every nook and cranny of a mysterious place like this!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Chests of hidden Mora — gotta find 'em all!

response.speaker: Idyia
response.text: Aha! I mean truly appreciating this place, not just wandering around it.

response.speaker: Idyia
response.text: Though if it's treasure you're interested in, why not give the "Returning Curios" project a try? It's an old tradition of our newly revitalized Veluriyam Mirage.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Returning... Curiosity? Why hasn't Paimon heard you mention this before?

response.speaker: Idyia
response.text: "Returning Curios," as the name indicates, refers to the multitude of fantastical items that have been swept into the vortex and funneled into the Veluriyam Mirage.

response.speaker: Idyia
response.text: This project goes back many a year. Originally, a veteran adventurer stopped here and was deeply moved by the scenery.

response.speaker: Idyia
response.text: *ahem* It goes without saying that my hospitality helped considerably.

response.speaker: Idyia
response.text: Anyway, he buried his most prized possessions in the place that touched him most deeply. Those were his "Mementos" — three pocket watches made of Mora.

response.speaker: Idyia
response.text: Before leaving, the adventurer left a poetic cipher and asked me to tell it to later guests, to see if they could find it.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Watches made of Mo—Mora? Sounds shiny! And valuable!

response.speaker: Idyia
response.text: I don't know how valuable they are, but when I mentioned it to later guests, they were even more excited than Paimon. They swore to retrieve the treasures left by that adventurer!

response.speaker: Idyia
response.text: Unfortunately, though they searched the whole Veluriyam Mirage, they were still unable to find the treasure trove hidden by the cipher.

response.speaker: Idyia
response.text: But in the process of searching, many guests began to relax and enjoy themselves, and lost all traces of the nervousness they had when they first entered the Mirage.

response.speaker: Idyia
response.text: Though they never found the adventurer's treasure, they found the idea fascinating, and chose to leave behind their own gifts in the Mirage, burying their stories and entrusting me with their care.

response.speaker: Idyia
response.text: In the end, though I never expected this, it has become a sort of tradition here.

response.speaker: Idyia
response.text: This is "Returning Curios" — Deciphering ciphers to reveal the treasures of guests' past! And then, passing down our own stories.

choices.text: What about the watches?

response.speaker: Idyia
response.text: Ah... haha... Now that you mention it... what did happen to the watches...?

response.speaker: Idyia
response.text: I only remember the stories he wanted to tell. Uh, right... what was the cipher again? Give me a moment, let me check to see if there are any records...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Idyia! Didn't you promise the adventurer? You need to be more reliable!

response.speaker: Idyia
response.text: Don't blame me! It was ages ago. There's been so many guests since then too, just stories upon stories... how can anyone expect me to memorize everything?

response.speaker: Idyia
response.text: Anyway, it's not about the value of the treasure or the watch, but the stories hidden inside the treasures!

response.speaker: Idyia
response.text: Yes, that's it! As long as the stories live on, treasures and such are just the cherry on top!

response.speaker: Idyia
response.text: Wh-What do you think? Would you like to join the tradition of Returning Curios? After all, the special Memento you leave will be retrieved by someone else in the far future.

response.speaker: Idyia
response.text: Imagine how that person will react to seeing your story, and the Memento you chose to leave behind, here and now... it's really fun, isn't it?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Paimon guesses it... kinda makes sense. Leaving gifts and secret messages behind for strangers sounds interesting, and solving riddles to look for hidden treasures makes Paimon giddy!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Ideally, we'll also get a ton of Mora while we're at it.

choices.text: After all, a gem ringed with gold is much prettier.

response.speaker: Idyia
response.text: Don't sweat it! According to the rules of old, each guest can hear one cipher and find one treasure.

response.speaker: Idyia
response.text: As you're my special guests, I'll give you three tries. Each cipher matches one of the treasure troves. And besides the stories told by each Memento, there's plenty of Mora to be found as well!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Good, good! That's perfect, Idyia!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: #Paimon doesn't know how impressive this mysterious adventurer was, but they couldn't be better than Paimon and {NICKNAME}.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Let's help continue this tradition too! We can bury a story here that belongs only to us, then we can think about what Memento and cipher to leave while we search!

response.speaker: Idyia
response.text: Then it's settled! Right, listen carefully to the first cipher...

response.speaker: Idyia
response.text: "A sweet mist permeates all, gazing toward the dancing lamplight, I almost forget to breathe. In the end, memories of childhood guide me, and I take my seat beside the table in peace..."

response.speaker: Idyia
response.text: Okay, the Returning Curios journey has begun! Remember the cipher, try hard to solve it, and locate the treasure!

choices.text: And my romanticism needs a reasonable reimbursement.
Were they ever found?
Maybe there's a huge trove of treasure.

dialogues.text: (These etchings are old...)

dialogues.speaker: Leave Message

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: The torches all went out. Do we need to light them in some specific order?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Gah. If only there were some way to see what the order should be...

dialogues.speaker: Idyia
dialogues.text: Back so soon? Such skilled treasure hunters!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Haha, the first cipher was too easy. We knew where to go immediately!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: But... what was with the Memento inside the chest?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: It seems like... it's from a person who gets hungry easily and stands outside restaurants enticed by the smell of food. The Memento is their snack bag, right?

dialogues.speaker: Idyia
dialogues.text: You're not completely wrong, but not totally right either.

dialogues.speaker: Idyia
dialogues.text: The traveler who left this first chest was a disciplined warrior.

dialogues.speaker: Idyia
dialogues.text: When I saw him in the desert, he was covered in wounds great and small. It was clear he had survived a bitter struggle.

dialogues.speaker: Idyia
dialogues.text: A tired, hungry person would obviously be drawn to the smell of a restaurant! It makes sense such circumstances would inspire written words, even a few lines of poetry.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Whoa! That's actually really different from what we thought...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Why was he fighting in the desert?

dialogues.speaker: Idyia
dialogues.text: If I speak too much, and add my own interpretations, it will color your perceptions and you won't experience their story as they wanted it told.

dialogues.speaker: Idyia
dialogues.text: The Memento still has his notes. Take some time to read them if you're curious.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: #Okay, fine. In that case, {NICKNAME}, you read it when you have time, and then tell Paimon the important bits.

dialogues.speaker: Idyia
dialogues.text: Let's move on, I want to share the cipher for the next treasure trove.

dialogues.speaker: Idyia
dialogues.text: "A shooting star of vines carries me, traversing a forest so quiet and peaceful, to finally arrive in secluded dreamland so pure."

dialogues.speaker: Idyia
dialogues.text: What do you think? This one will keep you guessing. Activate all those smarts of yours and find the second treasure trove!

dialogues.text: Took you longer this time, huh. Guess you're enjoying solving the riddles!

dialogues.speaker: Idyia
dialogues.text: So, what did you find besides Mora?

choices.text: Just a simple box.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Can we open it? But what if there's a creepy doll that pops out? Or fireworks that burst out with a bang!

response.speaker: Idyia
response.text: Oooh, yes, adding surprises to Mementos is a great idea. I'll suggest it to other guests too!

response.speaker: Idyia
response.text: But in this case, this is the standard box that I provide to guests. The guest that left this behind was quite serious, though, so you can rest assured there are no shenanigans!

response.speaker: Idyia
response.text: She was a lost student who woke up one day and found herself in the middle of the desert. She stumbled across the Veluriyam Mirage whilst searching for landmarks.

response.speaker: Idyia
response.text: It seemed like she hadn't finished her schoolwork, so she couldn't stay long. I was flustered too, unable to show her proper hospitality. Even now, I feel guilty about it...

response.speaker: Idyia
response.text: Luckily, her standards were really low! Just sitting in a quiet place stargazing was enough. Her other request was to have a closed, secluded environment to rest in.

response.speaker: Idyia
response.text: So I found a cave for her. Before she left, I even installed a door there that could be closed whenever she wanted undisturbed sleep!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: No wonder the cipher mentioned a dreamland. No one would bother you sleeping in a cave like that!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: But waking up in a strange place... that sounds familiar.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Maybe as she was sleeping on a carriage, and got thrown off? Perhaps by a grouchy driver?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: As Idyia said, Paimon thinks it would be best to wait until we've cleared our heads, then we can try tackling the tale of the mysterious student again!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: #There's just one chest left to find now! Come on, {NICKNAME}, let's finish these Returning Curios!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: If you really can't wait, go ahead and read it without Paimon! You're a fast reader, it should only take you a moment to read a couple pages.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Let me read it first, then I'll tell you everything.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Alright! With your storytelling, Paimon will be captivated!

response.speaker: Idyia
response.text: Ah! Dividing up the work with just a few words is a testament to your great and practiced teamwork.

response.speaker: Idyia
response.text: So let's continue the Returning Curios, shall we? Listen carefully to the third treasure's cipher...

response.speaker: Idyia
response.text: "A blue, spotless ceiling, a floor of white candy, soft companions surround me, I too have wings!"

response.speaker: Idyia
response.text: *ahem* Something so simple. Anyone would know where to go immediately!

response.speaker: Idyia
response.text: Well, it's easy to see, at least. Reaching it however...

response.speaker: Idyia
response.text: This should be fun to watch!

choices.text: Quite unremarkable.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Idyia, we're back!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: We succeeded, big time! All three treasures are ours!

dialogues.speaker: Idyia
dialogues.text: Well, well, well, someone's got a spring in their step! Isn't this treasure hunt quite special?

choices.text: It certainly was high enough up.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Whoever left that third treasure behind is a child at heart! They used creative metaphors, and their clues were right on the money.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Let Paimon guess, are they some kind of fairy tale author or something?

response.speaker: Idyia
response.text: Those aren't metaphors, they're just the real thoughts of a child. The one who left the third treasure behind was actually just a young girl.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Wait, a kid? You're joking, right?

choices.text: How did she even get up here?

response.speaker: Idyia
response.text: That child overheard her parents talking about a hidden paradise up in the clouds, where all sorts of beautiful creatures like finches and Crystalflies lived. So, she secretly built a big kite, hoping to soar into the clouds and visit her flying friends.

response.speaker: Idyia
response.text: I don't know if it was because the wind was ignorant, or if it was intentional, but the kite ended up being carried off course. Instead of soaring up to the paradise in the sky, it landed right in front of my house.

response.speaker: Idyia
response.text: The child didn't find her finches and Crystalflies, but she had a wonderful time playing with the gentle Hydro Eidolons, who became her squishy new friends.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Whoa, slow down there! You talk so fast that Paimon can hardly keep up!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: And... for a kid to fly all that way on a giant kite, a lot must have happened along the way. You're going too fast, and it seems like we're missing out on a lot of details.

response.speaker: Idyia
response.text: Look, I really can't explain the sense of wonder that kids feel during their adventures, so you'll just have to experience it for yourselves!

response.speaker: Idyia
response.text: Besides the message from the child, there are also a few pages from her diary in the box, and the details are really something.

response.speaker: Idyia
response.text: But before we get to that, there's still one things left to do that is both full of ceremony, but also quite important. Shall we take care of that first?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Yes, you're right! We've found all the treasures, so now it's time to leave a treasure of our own behind.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: #It's finally time! Let's put our heads together, {NICKNAME}. Where would be the perfect spot to bury our treasure?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: We have to think this through carefully. We can't be scatterbrained about it!

choices.text: How about the rooftop garden?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: A spot up high, huh? Sounds like a plan!

response.speaker: Idyia
response.text: Hiding it up somewhere high is a great choice! The views and experiences along the way will be truly unforgettable.

response.speaker: Idyia
response.text: And of course, mastering the art of scaling difficult terrain is a skill worth learning.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Yeah, we should definitely consider the route. Let's not put it in a spot that's too steep, or else the next guest might not be able to make it up there.

choices.text: The greater the challenge, the more satisfying the reward.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: That's a good point! It's like how a big meal tastes better after a hard day of work!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Solving riddles and finding treasures is so satisfying!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Rooftop garden it is, then. Let's head out!

response.speaker: Idyia
response.text: Hold on, please take this first!

response.speaker: Idyia
response.text: This is a special box imbued with the power of the Hydro Eidolons, which can greatly extend the storage time of Mementos and prevent them from deteriorating over time.

response.speaker: Idyia
response.text: And as for the Memento you choose, you can keep it a secret from me if you want.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Awesome! This really helps!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: With a fantastic container like this, we can store fresh things like fresh fruit and herbs and yummy food for a long time...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: But if we don't tell everything to Idyia... Will you still be able to pass along the cipher to other guests?

response.speaker: Idyia
response.text: It's all about mystery and surprise!

response.speaker: Idyia
response.text: As the treasure left behind by my most cherished guests, your Memento will be the crown jewel of the Returning Curios project, every bit as impressive as the original Mora Pocketwatch!

response.speaker: Idyia
response.text: I can't wait to see what kind of guest will find your treasure and how they'll react to your Memento...

response.speaker: Idyia
response.text: Will I be able to tell at a glance that this keepsake was left by you?

response.speaker: Idyia
response.text: I'm getting so excited!

choices.text: Idyia has given us so many surprises.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Oh, Paimon understands now...

response.speaker: Paimon

dialogues.text: #Let's look around, {NICKNAME}. Maybe we can find some way to open the door!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Idyia, we're back!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: We succeeded, big time! All three treasures are ours!

dialogues.speaker: Idyia
dialogues.text: Oh, that fast? I knew you were no ordinary person, but I didn't expect it to be this easy... How was your experience? Special?

choices.text: It certainly was high enough up.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Whoever left that third treasure behind is a child at heart! They used creative metaphors, and their clues were right on the money.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Let Paimon guess, are they some kind of fairy tale author or something?

response.speaker: Idyia
response.text: Those aren't metaphors, they're just the real thoughts of a child. The one who left the third treasure behind was actually just a young girl.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Wait, a kid? You're joking, right?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: How did she even get up here?

response.speaker: Idyia
response.text: That child overheard her parents talking about a hidden paradise up in the clouds, where all sorts of beautiful creatures like finches and Crystalflies lived. So, she secretly built a big kite, hoping to soar into the clouds and visit her flying friends.

response.speaker: Idyia
response.text: I don't know if it was because the wind was ignorant, or if it was intentional, but the kite ended up being carried off course. Instead of soaring up to the paradise in the sky, it landed in the middle of the desert.

response.speaker: Idyia
response.text: The child didn't find her finches and Crystalflies, but she had a wonderful time playing with the gentle Hydro Eidolons, who became her squishy new friends.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Whoa, slow down there! You talk so fast that Paimon can hardly keep up!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: And... for a kid to fly all that way on a giant kite, a lot must have happened along the way. You're going too fast, and it seems like we're missing out on a lot of details.

response.speaker: Idyia
response.text: Look, I really can't explain the sense of wonder that kids feel during their adventures, so you'll just have to experience it for yourselves!

response.speaker: Idyia
response.text: Besides the message from the child, there are also a few pages from her diary in the box, and the details are really something.

response.speaker: Idyia
response.text: But before we get to that, there's still one things left to do that is both full of ceremony, but also quite important. Shall we take care of that first?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Yes, you're right! We've found all the treasures, so now it's time to leave a treasure of our own behind.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: #It's finally time! Let's put our heads together, {NICKNAME}. Where would be the perfect spot to bury our treasure?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: We have to think this through carefully. We can't be scatterbrained about it!

choices.text: Great scenery on the way, though.

dialogues.speaker: Idyia
dialogues.text: Consider it a beautiful accident.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: The door opened! Whew, that was kinda tricky.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: #Huh, looks like Wolfgang hasn't written any notes here yet, {NICKNAME}...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: So he hasn't been here...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: We did open the chamber for him back then... This means he won't get stuck now, right?

choices.text: Well, if that device can be triggered multiple times...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Wait, then... Um, why don't we leave him a message?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: We'll leave it in an obvious place and tell him how to decipher the mechanism!

choices.text: Even if we did solve it once...

dialogues.speaker: Leave Message
dialogues.text: Let's leave a few words here, he should be able to see 'em!

dialogues.speaker: Leave Message
dialogues.text: Let's go back to the island outside the dream, maybe the notes are already gone!

dialogues.speaker: Leave Message
dialogues.text: (These etchings are fresh...)

dialogues.speaker: Leave Message
dialogues.text: (They describe how one may light the torches up in the right order...)

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: This notebook... Oh, it's "Wolfgang."

choices.text: Oh, joy. Stuck again, isn't he?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Paimon guesses some people need some punishment before they'll learn anything...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: #These underwater buildings... should be the mountain ruins within the dream... Let's go inside again to make sure, {NICKNAME}.

choices.text: Didn't learn his lesson, I suppose?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Well, that door closed, just as expected.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: This is the second chamber to trap Wolfgang. Let's see how we can get outta here.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Ahh! The door suddenly closed! Doesn't look like there's a switch, either.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Um, there's no other way out...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh, so this is the place...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Isn't this where we got blocked last time, and Wolfgang before us?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wolfgang's notebook isn't here either. Looks like he hasn't arrived yet.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Let's leave him some hints on how to open this secret chamber again, shall we?

choices.text: This solution...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Oh yeah, that's true. If Wolfgang can't make use of the elements...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Then the solution's useless to him. What should we do...

choices.text: How about we just make him not enter this place at all?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Ooh, that's right! We can just leave a hint outside saying that there's a secret chamber here.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Then he won't come in, and he won't get trapped in these ruins!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: C'mon, let's do it, quick!

choices.text: Let's leave a message outside the door.
Without the use of elemental powers...

dialogues.speaker: Message
dialogues.text: He should have gone into the secret chamber by the time he sees this message. Paimon thinks it won't be of that much use here...

dialogues.speaker: Leave Message
dialogues.text: This place should be eye-catching enough!

dialogues.speaker: Leave Message
dialogues.text: Let's hope Wolfgang does see it, and doesn't go running around the secret chambers in these ruins anymore...

dialogues.speaker: Leave Message
dialogues.text: Let's go back and have a look. Maybe his notes might have changed this time, too!

dialogues.speaker: Leave Message
dialogues.text: (These etchings are fresh...)

dialogues.speaker: Leave Message
dialogues.text: (They speak of how this place is a perilous secret chamber...)

dialogues.speaker: Leave Message
dialogues.text: (These etchings are old...)

dialogues.speaker: Leave Message
dialogues.text: (They speak of how this place is a perilous secret chamber...)

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Well, he didn't go in again. That's a relief.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Still, his annoyingly arrogant attitude is really ticking Paimon off!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: He really does sound like he's getting more and more full of himself...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: That said, the highland ruins he mentioned should be near the submerged ruins...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Let's take a look. Who knows if he was able to climb so high safely...

dialogues.speaker: Etchings
dialogues.text: (These etchings are old. They have been written as follows...)

dialogues.speaker: Etchings
dialogues.text: "The wind is very strong here, so I'm not going to use a notebook."

dialogues.speaker: Etchings
dialogues.text: "The sunrise here is beautiful indeed. It fills my heart with satisfaction to have braved many dangers to get here."

dialogues.speaker: Etchings
dialogues.text: "I wonder if anyone will come after me to see these same sights."

dialogues.speaker: Etchings
dialogues.text: "Now that I've cleared this particular trial... Next stop, Dragonspine!"

dialogues.speaker: Etchings
dialogues.text: "It's nice here, but it's a crying shame that there's no Mondstadt Hashbrowns..."

dialogues.speaker: Etchings
dialogues.text: "Wolfgang."

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Ooh, so there weren't any notes here because he carved a message on the pillar. Huh, so he made it all the way here.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Where does his confidence come from, though... If we hadn't helped him out, he'd still be stuck in the secret chamber!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: He's pretty much gonna be Chilled Meat if he goes to Dragonspine!

choices.text: That's a little overboard...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Eh? U—Um, Paimon just means that he'd be in deep trouble if he went to Dragonspine.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: We need to tell him not to go, and quick!

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Well, let's leave him another message, shall we...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Right, that's right! Paimon thinks so too... And y'know what, let's leave him some Mondstadt Hash Browns this time!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Maybe he'll start missing the warmth of Mondstadt once he's had a bite, and he'll give up on going to Dragonspine!

choices.text: Well, he's going to get in trouble for sure.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Exactly! Dragonspine's super cold and is filled with hilichurls... Not to mention The Great Snowboar King!

dialogues.speaker: Leave Message
dialogues.text: Let's leave our message here — and a Mondstadt Hash Brown too!

dialogues.speaker: Leave Message
dialogues.text: Paimon really hopes that Wolfgang can give that notion of going to Dragonspine a rest...

dialogues.speaker: Leave Message
dialogues.text: Let's go to the ruins we were at before once we leave the dream. Maybe we'll find some sign of him changing his mind!

dialogues.speaker: Leave Message
dialogues.text: (These etchings are fresh...)

dialogues.speaker: Leave Message
dialogues.text: "Do not go to Dragonspine. It is a perilous place..."

dialogues.speaker: Leave Message
dialogues.text: (These etchings are old...)

dialogues.speaker: Leave Message
dialogues.text: "Do not go to Dragonspine. It is a perilous place..."

dialogues.speaker: Etchings
dialogues.text: (These etchings are old. They have been written as follows...)

dialogues.speaker: Etchings
dialogues.text: "The wind is very strong here, so I'm not going to use a notebook."

dialogues.speaker: Etchings
dialogues.text: "Haha, to think that I'd find a Hash Brown here — and still warm, too! It's practically a miracle."

dialogues.speaker: Etchings
dialogues.text: "Many thanks to whoever etched the messages. Your Hash Brown is the best I've ever tasted."

dialogues.speaker: Etchings
dialogues.text: "And thank you. I do know that Dragonspine is very dangerous... and I know my limits as well. But I must go."

dialogues.speaker: Etchings
dialogues.text: "Who knows, a sign that says 'here be traps' might be the only remnant of my journey to Dragonspine."

dialogues.speaker: Etchings
dialogues.text: "But if someone else can avoid that danger and get further than I did, that to me would be something even more precious than a Hash Brown."

dialogues.speaker: Etchings
dialogues.text: "Thank you, etcher of messages. But we adventurers exist precisely because of perils like Dragonspine."

dialogues.speaker: Etchings
dialogues.text: "Dearest Regards, Wolfgang."

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: What the... This guy's saying some pretty glib stuff, huh?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: This is bad. We've got to get to Dragonspine and...

choices.text: Paimon, we can only change his past as it exists inside the dream...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Ah... Right, that's true. The entire Golden Apple Archipelago is under the effects of the dream...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: That's why Paimon thought that he was rescued... But in the end, he really was just stuck in that secret chamber, wasn't he...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: But still, this Wolfgang is really... annoying! We helped him so much, but he still thinks that it would be nice if he could "pave the way" for others...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Couldn't he at least value his life a little more?

choices.text: Everybody's looking for that something...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Paimon knows, it's just... Paimon feels bad for him, that's all.

choices.text: Something more important than their own life...
Wolfgang will never make it to Dragonspine...
